question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the exponential term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{2}(0.43)^{4x+5}+4 & >-2 \\ \frac{3}{2}(0.43)^{4x+5} & >-6 \\ (0.43)^{4x+5} & >-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, recall that a positive number raised to any real power is always positive. Since $0.43>0,$ we have

$$
(0.43)^{4x+5}>0
$$

for every real value of $x.$

In particular, every value of $(0.43)^{4x+5}$ is greater than $-4.$ Therefore,

$$
(0.43)^{4x+5}>-4
$$

for all real values of $x.$

Hence, the original inequality is satisfied for all real numbers.
